title: Alberta NDP win in Calgary-Shaw byelection
summary: Unofficial results from Elections Alberta show NDP candidate Kyle Campbell has won Calgary-Shaw by a margin of 582 votes over the UCP's Mike Derry.

image.caption: Calgary-Shaw candidate Kyle Campbell and Alberta NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi celebrate the party's byelection win at a pub in southeast Calgary on Monday evening. The NDP won by a margin of 582 votes. (Nait Luit/CBC)

blocks.text: Unofficial results from Elections Alberta show NDP candidate Kyle Campbell has won Calgary-Shaw by a margin of 582 votes over the UCP's Mike Derry.
Kyle Campbell won by a margin of 582 votes, unofficial results show
Alberta NDP candidate Kyle Campbell has won the byelection in Calgary-Shaw, unofficial results from Elections Alberta show.
With all polls reporting, Campbell earned 7,461 of 16,002 votes counted, or about 47 per cent of the vote, 582 votes ahead of the UCP candidate Mike Derry.
Campbell's win represents the first time the NDP has won the riding since 2015, with the UCP winning it in 2019 and 2023.
The seat has been vacant since its previous representative, UCP MLA and former cabinet minister Rebecca Schulz, resigned earlier this year, triggering the byelection.
Official results will be confirmed on Sept. 24.
